title: Suspected Rheumatoid Arthritis: Primary Care Recognition and Early Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult primary-care recognition, initial investigation and urgent rheumatology referral for suspected persistent synovitis.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national rheumatoid arthritis guideline was identified in the sources opened on 14 October 2026. NICE guidance is an international comparator pending Saudi/local adaptation.
SFDA product registration was not verified; any medicine selection requires the current Saudi Drug Information register and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Autoimmune synovial inflammation causes pain, swelling and stiffness. Persistent inflammation can erode cartilage and bone. Small joints of the hands and feet are commonly involved. Systemic inflammation can affect organs outside the joints.
keyMechanisms: Autoimmune synovial inflammation causes pain, swelling and stiffness.
Persistent inflammation can erode cartilage and bone.
Small joints of the hands and feet are commonly involved.
Systemic inflammation can affect organs outside the joints.

references.title: NICE NG100: Rheumatoid arthritis in adults: management

symptoms: Persistent joint pain, swelling and morning stiffness; ask about duration, function and symmetry.
physicalSigns: Clinical synovitis: soft swelling, warmth, tenderness and restricted movement; examine hands, feet and other symptomatic joints.
redFlags: Septic-joint features, systemic illness, rapidly progressive neurological deficit or vasculitic/organ-threatening features need same-day escalation.
precipitants: Smoking, family history and established autoimmune disease increase suspicion; symptoms may begin without a clear trigger.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Bony enlargement and activity-related pain without persistent soft synovitis.
Abrupt hot monoarthritis; aspirate urgently when infection is possible.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Persistent soft-tissue swelling, warmth and restricted movement
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Refer on clinical suspicion; normal blood tests do not remove the need.

clinicalManagement.title: Exclude an acute joint emergency
actions: If a hot joint or systemic illness suggests infection, use the same-day septic-joint pathway.
Document the number and distribution of swollen joints and functional impact.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer suspected persistent synovitis
actions: Refer urgently when small hand/foot joints or more than one joint are affected, or when presentation was delayed by 3 months or more.
Request blood tests and hand/foot radiographs without delaying referral.

clinicalManagement.title: Safety-net pending review
actions: Advise urgent reassessment for fever, a rapidly hot swollen joint, neurological deficit or major functional deterioration.
Record tobacco exposure, pregnancy possibility, comorbidity and current medicines for treatment planning.

medicationPlan.note: Recognition and referral do not require initiation of a disease-modifying medicine in primary care; specialist treatment is covered in the linked DMARD topic.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Persistent synovitis affecting small hand/foot joints, more than one joint, or delay of 3 months or longer from symptom onset to seeking advice.

teaching.scope: Adult primary-care recognition, initial investigation and urgent rheumatology referral for suspected persistent synovitis.
pitfalls: Treating a possible septic joint as chronic inflammatory arthritis.
keyPoints: Normal inflammatory markers or negative rheumatoid factor do not exclude rheumatoid arthritis.
Small-joint or multi-joint synovitis warrants urgent referral.

references.title: NICE NG100: Rheumatoid arthritis in adults: management

patientEducation: Explain that early specialist treatment protects function and that normal tests do not rule out disease.
lifestyleAndDiet: Support smoking cessation and activity within pain limits.
mdtReferrals: Rheumatology; physiotherapy or occupational therapy after assessment.
dischargeCriteria: Not discharged from follow-up until the referral outcome and safety-net are documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Track referral completion and reassess sooner if swelling, systemic illness or function worsens.
